00001| // The runtime obligation tree an answer must discharge before it may finish
00002| // (rust/src/obligation_ledger.rs, rust/src/obligation_ledger/derivation.rs).

00004| // Shapes (Rust enum -> tagged object):

00006| //   `{kind: 'command_exit', command, expected_exit}`, `{kind: 'output_hash',
00007| //   command, sha256}`, `{kind: 'symbolic_check', check_id}`,

00034| /** Mirrors `fn clauses_with_spans`: `[clause, [start, end]]` in UTF-8 bytes. */
00035| export function clausesWithSpans(request) {
00036|   const cues = wordsForRole('enumeration_cue');
00037|   if (!cues.length) return [[trim(request), [0, utf8Len(request)]]];

00039|   for (let index = 0; index < request.length; index += request.codePointAt(index) > 0xffff ? 2 : 1) {
00040|     if (index === 0 || !opensAClause(request, index)) continue;

00042|     if (cues.some((cue) => startsWithCue(rest, cue))) boundaries.push(index);
00043|   }
00044|   boundaries.push(request.length);
00045|   const unique = boundaries.filter((value, at) => at === 0 || value !== boundaries[at - 1]);
00046|   const out = [];
00047|   for (let at = 0; at + 1 < unique.length; at += 1) {
00048|     const raw = request.slice(unique[at], unique[at + 1]);
00049|     const trimmed = trim(raw);

00059|  * cue opening a new line cuts even when the previous line ends without a

00062| function opensAClause(request, index) {
00063|   const lineEnd = trimEndMatches(request.slice(0, index), (character) => [' ', '\t', '\r'].includes(character));
00064|   const before = trimEnd(lineEnd);

00068| /** @param {string} character */
00069| function isUnspacedScript(character) {
00070|   const cp = character.codePointAt(0);
00071|   return (cp >= 0x3040 && cp <= 0x30ff) || (cp >= 0x3400 && cp <= 0x4dbf) || (cp >= 0x4e00 && cp <= 0x9fff)

00131| /** Mirrors `fn derive_expectation`. */
00132| export function deriveExpectation(clause) {
00133|   const plan = composeGeneralChangePlan(clause);
00134|   if (plan !== null) {
00135|     return shapeFor(plan, expectationRules().find((rule) => rule.when === 'general_plan_mode' && rule.mode === plan.mode) ?? null);

00176| /** Mirrors `ObligationNode::build`. */

00178|   const root = leafNode(null, request, [0, utf8Len(request)], 0, deriveExpectation(request));

00193| function expand(node, maxSplitDepth) {

00196|   if (pieces.length < 2) return;

00210|     expand(child, maxSplitDepth);
00211|     children.push(child);

00001| //! Reading a request's clauses, and each clause's expectation, out of data.
00002| //!
00003| //! Plan 05 leaves 5, 6 and 7 own this file. The clause splitter is the one
00004| //! `task_obligations` already splits on — the seeded enumeration cues — and the
00005| //! expectation derivation is the rule set of
00006| //! `data/meta/obligation-evidence-contract.lino`, so a new expectation shape is a
00007| //! data edit rather than a `match` arm here.
00008| 
00009| use crate::agentic_coding::general_planner::GeneralChangePlan;
00010| use crate::engine::stable_id;
00011| 
00012| use super::ObligationExpectation;
00013| 
00014| /// The clauses a request enumerates, each with its UTF-8 byte span in the
00015| /// request exactly as the user wrote it.
00016| ///
00017| /// The cut points are the seeded enumeration cues — the same role
00018| /// `task_obligations` already splits on — but a cue only cuts where it *opens* a
00019| /// clause: at the start of the request, or just after a sentence ends. A "first"
00020| /// inside "whose first line is exactly `---`" describes a file's contents and
00021| /// opens nothing (issue #1099).
00022| ///
00023| /// The sentence terminators include `。`, `！`, `？` and `।` beside the Latin
00024| /// ones, because a Chinese or Hindi request ends its sentences with those and a
00025| /// splitter that does not know them reads five languages as one clause.
00026| #[must_use]
00027| pub fn clauses_with_spans(request: &str) -> Vec<(String, (usize, usize))> {
00028|     let cues = crate::seed::lexicon().words_for_role(crate::seed::ROLE_ENUMERATION_CUE);
00029|     if cues.is_empty() {
00030|         return vec![(request.trim().to_owned(), (0, request.len()))];
00031|     }
00032|     let mut boundaries = vec![0_usize];
00033|     for (index, _) in request.char_indices() {
00034|         if index == 0 || !opens_a_clause(request, index) {
00035|             continue;
00036|         }
00037|         let rest = request[index..].to_lowercase();
00038|         if cues.iter().any(|cue| starts_with_cue(&rest, cue)) {
00039|             boundaries.push(index);
00040|         }
00041|     }
00042|     boundaries.push(request.len());
00043|     boundaries.dedup();
00044|     boundaries
00045|         .windows(2)
00046|         .filter_map(|window| {
00047|             let raw = &request[window[0]..window[1]];
00048|             let trimmed = raw.trim();
00049|             if trimmed.is_empty() {
00050|                 return None;
00051|             }
00052|             let start = window[0] + raw.find(trimmed)?;
00053|             Some((trimmed.to_owned(), (start, start + trimmed.len())))
00054|         })
00055|         .collect()
00056| }
00057| 
00058| /// Whether the byte at `index` begins a clause: everything before it either ends
00059| /// a sentence, ends a line, or is nothing but whitespace.
00060| ///
00061| /// The line break is read before trimming: `trim_end` would strip it, and a cue
00062| /// opening a new line ("…\"Alpha\"\nThen, print …") would never cut (issue
00063| /// #1166).
00064| fn opens_a_clause(request: &str, index: usize) -> bool {
00065|     let line_end = request[..index].trim_end_matches([' ', '\t', '\r']);
00066|     let before = line_end.trim_end();
00067|     before.is_empty()
00068|         || line_end.ends_with('\n')
00069|         || before.ends_with(['.', '!', '?', ';', ':', '。', '！', '？', '।', '॥'])
00070| }
00071| 
00072| /// Whether `rest` opens with `cue` as a whole word — or, for a script that does
00073| /// not space its words, as its own leading run of characters.
00074| ///
00075| /// The word-boundary test is only meaningful where words are spaced. `然后确认`
00076| /// is a cue followed immediately by the verb it introduces, and `确` is
00077| /// alphanumeric, so demanding a non-alphanumeric follower reads Chinese and
00078| /// Japanese as one clause and every enumerated obligation in those languages is
00079| /// silently merged into the first.
00080| fn starts_with_cue(rest: &str, cue: &str) -> bool {
00081|     let Some(after) = rest.strip_prefix(cue) else {
00082|         return false;
00083|     };
00084|     if cue.chars().any(is_unspaced_script) {
00085|         return true;
00086|     }
00087|     after
00088|         .chars()
00089|         .next()
00090|         .is_none_or(|character| !character.is_alphanumeric())
00091| }
00092| 
00093| /// Whether a character belongs to a script that does not separate its words with
00094| /// spaces: the CJK ideographs, the kana, and the Hangul syllables.
00095| const fn is_unspaced_script(character: char) -> bool {
00096|     matches!(character,
00097|         '\u{3040}'..='\u{30ff}'
00098|             | '\u{3400}'..='\u{4dbf}'
00099|             | '\u{4e00}'..='\u{9fff}'
00100|             | '\u{ac00}'..='\u{d7af}'
00101|             | '\u{f900}'..='\u{faff}')
00102| }

00104| /// Read one clause's expectation out of the clause itself.
00105| ///
00106| /// The composer that already plans a standalone request is the authority on what
00107| /// artifact a clause names; when it reads one, the plan's own mode says which
00108| /// shape of observation would settle the clause. When it reads none, a clause
00109| /// that still names an observable action is a symbolic check, and a clause that
00110| /// names neither is `Underivable` — kept, split, and finally reported, never
00111| /// discarded.
00112| #[must_use]
00113| pub fn derive_expectation(clause: &str) -> ObligationExpectation {
00114|     let rules = ExpectationRules::shipped();
00115|     if let Some(plan) = crate::agentic_coding::general_planner::compose_general_change_plan(clause)
00116|     {
00117|         let rule = rules.for_plan_mode(plan.mode.slug());
00118|         return shape_for(&plan, rule);
00119|     }
00120|     if crate::task_decomposition::is_checkable(clause) {
00121|         let rule = rules.for_generated_check();
00122|         if rule.is_none_or(|rule| rule.expectation == "symbolic_check") {
00123|             return ObligationExpectation::SymbolicCheck {
00124|                 check_id: format!(
00125|                     "obligation:{}",
00126|                     stable_id("obligation_check", clause.trim())
00127|                 ),
00128|             };
00129|         }
00130|     }
00131|     ObligationExpectation::Underivable {
00132|         reason: rules
00133|             .for_absent_artifact()
00134|             .map_or_else(|| String::from("no_artifact_in_clause"), |rule| rule.reason),
00135|     }
00136| }

00138| /// Build the expectation a matched rule names out of the plan it matched.
00139| ///
00140| /// Hashing the observed bytes is only honest when the request states what they
00141| /// must be; when it does not, the rule's `otherwise` shape applies and the
00142| /// observable claim is the command's exit status, never a digest nothing
00143| /// declared (plan 05 risk 4).
00144| fn shape_for(plan: &GeneralChangePlan, rule: Option<ExpectationRule>) -> ObligationExpectation {
00145|     let Some(rule) = rule else {
00146|         return ObligationExpectation::Underivable {
00147|             reason: format!("no_rule_for_plan_mode_{}", plan.mode.slug()),
00148|         };
00149|     };
00150|     let declared = expected_digest(&plan.content);
00151|     let shape = match (&declared, rule.otherwise.as_deref()) {
00152|         (None, Some(otherwise)) => otherwise,
00153|         _ => rule.expectation.as_str(),
00154|     };
00155|     match shape {
00156|         "file_bytes" => ObligationExpectation::FileBytes {
00157|             path: plan.target.clone(),
00158|             sha256: declared,
00159|         },
00160|         "output_hash" => declared.map_or_else(
00161|             || ObligationExpectation::CommandExit {
00162|                 command: plan.verification_command.clone(),
00163|                 expected_exit: 0,
00164|             },
00165|             |sha256| ObligationExpectation::OutputHash {
00166|                 command: plan.verification_command.clone(),
00167|                 sha256,
00168|             },
00169|         ),
00170|         "command_exit" => ObligationExpectation::CommandExit {
00171|             command: plan.verification_command.clone(),
00172|             expected_exit: 0,
00173|         },
00174|         "symbolic_check" => ObligationExpectation::SymbolicCheck {
